deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Riemann's 1851 Göttingen dissertation ('Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'). The page corresponds to the published Art. 11. The final paragraph belongs to the Dirichlet-principle articles (published Art. 16-18). The previous page is the draft of the published Art. 10 (integrability of u dx - v dy, existence of the potential U). The next page is draft material on branch points (Windungspunkte) and the flux integral ∫∂u/∂p ds = -2π Σ(n-1).

(A) Mean-value property and the sign argument. Let u be harmonic (Δu = 0) in the simply connected surface T. Let O be an interior point with u(O) = u_0, and consider a circle of radius r about O lying in T, with polar angle φ. The previous article gave a_0 = (1/2π)∫_0^{2π} u dφ, the constant Fourier coefficient of u on the circle. Combined with a_0 = u_0, the value at the centre (the Gauss mean-value theorem; this identification is mine, as in the printed text), this gives
  ∫_0^{2π} (u - u_0) dφ = 0.
Riemann notes this is impossible if u - u_0 is positive on part of the circle and nowhere negative, or vice versa. So on every such circle, u - u_0 either vanishes identically or takes both signs.

(B) Under the same hypotheses on u and T as at the end of the previous article, three theorems follow.
 I. u cannot have a maximum or a minimum at an interior point of T. [Implicit, mine: if u_0 were an extremum, u - u_0 would be one-signed on all small circles about O. By (A) it would then vanish on them, so u would be constant near O. That case is excluded by II unless u is constant everywhere, so the statement is meant for non-constant u, i.e. it is the strong maximum principle.]
 II. u cannot be constant on one part of T and take a different value on another part. This is unique continuation, or the identity theorem for harmonic functions. No proof is given on this page; in print it rests on Art. 10, i.e. on real-analyticity of u, or on the circle argument.
 III. If u is given on a part of T, it is determined on all of T. Proof given: if u_1 and u_2 both satisfy the (linear) conditions imposed on u, so does u_1 - u_2. If they agreed on one part of T but not on another, then u_1 - u_2 would be 0 on the first part and nonzero on the second, contradicting II.

(C) Fragment of the Dirichlet principle (cf. published Art. 16-17). Put v = α + h, where h ranges over admissible functions. The Dirichlet-type integral Ω[v] is then finite, becomes infinite only together with L, varies continuously with h, and is never below 0. Riemann concludes ('folglich') that Ω attains a minimum for at least one shape of the function ω. That minimiser is then shown in print to be harmonic, which yields the existence of the desired function.
errors: The concluding inference in (C), 'Ω ≥ 0 and continuous in h, hence Ω has a minimum for some ω', is the famous gap in Riemann's use of the Dirichlet principle. A functional bounded below need not attain its infimum on an infinite-dimensional admissible class. Weierstrass gave a counterexample in 1870, ∫_{-1}^{1} x²φ'² dx with fixed boundary values different from each other. The gap was repaired by Hilbert (1900/1904) and later work.

Statement I, taken literally, fails for constant u. Read with II it means the strong maximum principle (no extremum unless u is constant). The mean-value argument directly gives only that u is constant near an extremal point; the global conclusion needs II.
Theorem II is asserted without proof on this page. It requires analyticity (Art. 10) or a connectedness argument, and T must be connected.
The step a_0 = u_0, needed to turn the Fourier-coefficient formula into ∫(u-u_0)dφ = 0, is taken from the previous article and not restated here. This is not an error, but it is implicit.

results.what: Values on a part of T determine a harmonic function on all of T, proved by linearity and II

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of Art. 11 and part of Art. 16-17 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation. The maximum principle, identity theorem and Dirichlet-principle argument, including its well-known gap, are all known to be his. The page's interest is only in showing the drafting process.

transcription_corrections: Final paragraph: 'bei mit h stetig ändert' should read 'sich mit h stetig ändert' (cf. printed Art. 16: 'sich mit der Gestalt von λ stetig ändert').

Final paragraph: the struck 'einen endlichen' together with the clause 'der [nur/nicht] mit L zugleich unendlich wird' corresponds to the printed 'einen endlichen Werth, der nur mit L zugleich unendlich wird'. The interlinear word read as 'nicht' is probably 'nur'.
Line 3: the interlinear insertion reads 'um einen Punkt O' (O, not the digit 0), referring to the circle described about the point O.
Line 4-5: the alternative wording appears to read 'oder irgendwo positiv oder negativ zu werden' as a variant of 'ohne irgendwo einen negativen zu erhalten'.
Theorem I: the word order with the inserted 'nicht' is 'kann im Innern in einem Punkte von T nicht ein Maximum oder ein Minimum haben'.
First line: 'Aus dem vorigen Art.' should probably read 'Die im vorigen Art. erhaltene Gl.' (the image begins with 'Die im vorigen Art.').
